# Veil 0.13.0

Stable release for all ten Veil, Shield Swap, and Bridge packages, published
under npm’s `latest` tag.

```sh
npm install @provablehq/veil-core@latest @provablehq/veil-aleo-sdk@latest
```

## Changes

- Generate compliance Merkle proofs automatically for Shield Swap actions and
  Bridge ARC-22 unshielding and private xReserve burns. Local SDK accounts check
  the current chain root and cache verified witnesses while that root is unchanged.
- Support wallet-derived freezelist requests and constrained algorithm grants.
  Preserve supplied proof strings, wallet requests, and existing provider callbacks;
  also accept action-sized tuples and annotated compliance proofs.
- Read Bridge compliance state through its required public client. Wallet adapters
  need only `executeTransaction`; account and proving metadata remain optional.
- Preserve opaque collect/rebalance calls with supplied proof tuples or custom
  providers without `withdrawalAddress`. Automatic generation and providers marked
  `requiresSubject` report an error when the actual address cannot be recovered.
- Allow public fee-tier discovery, matching the deployed Shield Swap API.

## Compliance

Proof generation is enabled by default in the Shield Swap and Bridge SDKs.
With a local SDK client or a compatible wallet connected with the required
algorithm grants, callers need no manual proof generation, provider, or cache.
Omit `proofs` (Shield Swap) or `merkleProof` (Bridge) to use the default.

| SDK | Public function | When Merkle exclusion proofs are required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shield Swap | `swap()`, `swapMultiHop()` | Wrapped input-token sender; intermediate hops add no proof inputs |
| Shield Swap | `claimSwapOutput()` | Shield Swap signer, plus wrapped output and refund receivers when applicable |
| Shield Swap | `mint()` | Shield Swap signer, position recipient, withdrawal address, and any wrapped token senders |
| Shield Swap | `increaseLiquidity()` | Wrapped token senders |
| Shield Swap | `collect()` | Shield Swap position owner, withdrawal address, and any wrapped token receivers |
| Shield Swap | `rebalancePosition()` | Shield Swap position owner and withdrawal address, funded wrapped token senders, and wrapped token receivers |
| Bridge | `bridge.unshield()` / exported `unshield()` | ARC-22 private-to-public transfer; one signer bundle |
| Bridge | `bridge.execute()` | Outbound Aleo USDCx xReserve burn in private mode (the default); one signer bundle |
| Bridge | `xreserve.aleoToEvm.execute()` | Standalone execution of the same private burn; one signer bundle |

A bundle is `[MerkleProof; 2]`, proving one address against one list. Credits
wrappers use placeholders without an exclusion check. Shield Swap
`decreaseLiquidity()` and `burn()`, Bridge ARC-20 unshielding, `bridge.shield()`,
and public xReserve burns require no exclusion proofs.

Explicit configuration is optional: supply encoded proof strings, ordered tuples,
annotated proofs, or a provider when the application needs control. Shield Swap
also supports a client-wide provider; `proofs: null` restores automatic generation.
Local accounts generate and cache proofs against the current root, including
when transaction proving is delegated. Compatible wallets derive proofs during
execution. Custom deployments need explicit freezelist mappings. Automatic
`collect()` and `rebalancePosition()` need `withdrawalAddress` when the position
record is opaque. Supplied proof tuples and custom providers keep the address
optional, except for providers marked `requiresSubject`.

The offline `buildXReserveBurnCall()` builder accepts a supplied bundle or inserts
a wallet request; use an execution function above for automatic local generation.
Core's `walletClient.transfer()` can accept `merkleProof` for compliant-token
private transfers and unshielding, but does not generate it automatically.

## Validation and known limitations

The regression suite passed 2,436 tests, with 275 gated tests skipped. All 32
type tests passed. All ten packages build and install together; installed Bridge
and first-swap examples compile.

Live testnet validation covered all four swap routes and eight liquidity tests.
The two-hop claim initially failed when the freezelist root changed in the same
block with a zero-block grace window. The route rerun and recovery claim both
succeeded with fresh proofs; all swaps were claimed. The mainnet Arc private burn
passed with a supplied proof string.

The mainnet Ethereum burn accepted automatically generated proofs and delivered
0.996501 USDC. Its delivery assertion failed because the existing registry assumes
a 2-USDC fee, while the provider charged 1.0035 USDC. This fee-quote discrepancy
remains unresolved. The mainnet freezelist was empty during this validation.

Automatic local generation requires the SDK generator. Wallet derivation requires
algorithm support and matching grants; custom deployments require explicit
freezelist mappings. Supplied proofs and providers remain responsible for freshness.
A root change can invalidate an in-flight proof when the contract provides no grace window;
retry a rejected claim with freshly resolved proofs.

A combined install including Bridge and optional Privy helpers may encounter their
existing Solana peer-version conflict. The package checks explicitly select
`@solana/kit@^8.0.0`.

Source: [feature PR #188](https://github.com/ProvableHQ/veil/pull/188) and
[release PR #189](https://github.com/ProvableHQ/veil/pull/189).
